title: Under Glaring Light
subtitle: No, not a coronal mass ejection—just an unexpected firework.

items.text: Under Glaring Light
Abandoned Research Station
Another equally forgotten research station.
Close enough, just a few slopes away. Yet it proves enough distance to put the crazed dogs off their chase.
The windows are drafty, the power dim and dying, but at least the air carries no stench of blood or decay.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Every room has been checked. There are no hidden enemies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you, Sonetto. Let's take a rest before we set off again.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: According to the official map, the previous station we entered is called Shackleton Station. It's supposed to be the site of the largest scientific research operation in a 70-mile radius.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If even they fell victim to such a tragedy, it's hard to imagine any of the smaller stations surviving it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There must be a purpose behind these attacks.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Judging from the state of the corpses, the researchers were sacrificed for some kind of ritual.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If we assume that Manus Vindictae did this—

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: There is no doubt. This was done by those Snow Monsters.
Nautika's muffled voice emerges from the corner. After their last encounter, she had been silent and still as if like a statue, but at last she begins to unpack jars and cans of food from her bag.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then it's highly likely that this was all in service of the same "ritual" Mr. Aleph mentioned.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: It's so cruel. What kind of ritual would require such a thing?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We have too little information to piece together the truth. But judging by this massacre, they need human sacrifices.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Or perhaps, they're eliminating any "aliens"—in this case, humans—in the vicinity before they perform the ritual.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: In any case, this shows how much this "ritual" means to them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If Dr. Dores was in fact here, then we're on the right track.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: According to Ms. Amundsen's map, we're not far at all from the central region. We must catch up with Dr. Dores before she enters Manus Vindictae territory.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: From the looks of the angle of the sun, we still have some time to catch up to her before it gets dark.
Nautika arranges the food by type and size, muttering under her breath.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Mother Spirit, thank you for feeding us and for everything you provide.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And, of course, thank you to Ms. Vertin and Ms. Sonetto for providing the food.
Their voices fall quiet for a time, replaced by the soft murmur of chewing and the slurp of canned food.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm glad to see you looking more calm.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Sorry. I wasn't always like this.
She stammers out an apology that gathers into an explanation.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I was ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: They said I was like a fearless sled dog.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Don't worry. I understand. We've all gone through things that have scarred us.
The incandescent lights flicker as if nodding in agreement.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Is it to do with what we saw in Shackleton Station?
She untangles her fingers with force.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I know you need information, but there isn't much else I can tell you.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Insanity, Snow Monsters, starvation ... Death just kept on coming. Friele told me to run, so I did. I ran all the way back the way we came.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I ran fast, as fast as I could. But when I got to the station, everyone had either left or ... *sigh*
She stops, unable to continue.
Words aren't necessary to piece together the rest of her story.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm sorry.
Nautika shakes her head. Meeting Sonetto's gaze, she steels herself and tries again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I don't know if it's because of hyperventilation or that I hit my head, but there are some things I can't remember clearly.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But that fear I felt—that fear still haunts me. I'm no longer as brave as I used to be.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Back in my hometown, you're considered brave if you can tame a reindeer. We have a racing festival every year.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Whoever wins the race serves as the voice of the Mother Spirit. They hear Her voice and beat its rhythm in praise of the sun, and the flag of our village is raised high into the sky to declare their victory.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I was the best dog-and-reindeer trainer of my age. I always thought I would be the one to beat the drum one day.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But now, even my sled dogs are gone. They were so brave to venture all the way to Antarctica with me.
Her eyes drop. The words still don't come.
Her fingers twist back together, untwist, then twist again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm not that girl anymore.
The air feels damp, damper than it has any right to be on this cold, dry continent.
Sonetto turns and pulls out a thick stack of documents meticulously organized, as always.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen, I thought you would like to see this.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: An expedition diary?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh! Did you take all these from Shackleton Station?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. Due to the urgency of the situation, we were only able to grab a few documents.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We thought you'd have liked to look through them, had we not encountered those rabid dogs, so we took what we could before we left.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: A Survey of the Antarctic Critter Biosphere, An Indexed Dictionary of Arcane Runes ... A Polar Guide to the Arcane Cultivation of Vegetables!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Incredible! Fantastic! With this, we may finally master how to grow potatoes in polar regions!
Under the dim light, Nautika's face flushes red with emotion.
A long time passes before she realizes she's been lost in her reading.
She gathers each precious page, then looks up at her new teammates. There's a conflict burning in her eyes.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Thank you. Thank you so much.
In the end, all she can manage is to repeat her thanks.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It was worth the risk.
The scent of canned food lingers as each savors both the fullness of their bellies and the rare moment of peace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are you looking at, Sonetto?
Sonetto closes the door, looking very grave.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The sun doesn't seem to have moved at all since we last calculated the angle, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Oh, is it the midnight sun? If only I had the eyes to see it.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Technically, it's autumn in Antarctica at the moment. Polar day only occurs in the summer months.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Indeed. We've seen it rise and fall several times since we left from Tierra del Fuego.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And even if it were the season for polar day, the solar angle would still vary.
Nautika's breathing once again picks up speed as their analysis progresses.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No. No, it can't be.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: All these abnormal phenomena, the sun standing still in the sky, that aurora in the broad daylight—
*boom*

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Agh!

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: What? What's that sound?

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Are we in an avalanche? No, it sounds like the screaming of critters.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, take a look at this.
They burst out from the station's door.
Weird creatures flap their wings in the cold wind, hissing desperately at the intruders.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's the Snow Monsters. Their flying beasts.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen, stay back.
With a piercing shriek, the Olitiau plummets from the sky.
And as if perfectly aligned, it lands square and heavy on their poor snowmobile.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No, no, no, no, no.
She dashes out, desperate to save the vehicle teetering on the edge of destruction, only to be held back by her companions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Don't—!
Flames shoot out first, followed by a screeching roar,
rising to its grand finale: a spectacular explosion.
The transmission tears free from the blast.
The snowmobile lies scattered across the white ice field, flames still licking over its spilled fuel tank.
Blinded by the smoke rising from the fire, they make out a glowing mass that brightens the endless daylight sky.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That was our only means of transportation.
